## 1. The golden rules

1. **Never push to `main`.** `main` is production and is protected. Only the owner releases to it.
2. **Never commit straight to `dev`.** `dev` is the shared integration branch. Your work reaches `dev` only through a **pull request** that has been reviewed and has green CI.
3. **One issue = one branch = one pull request.** Branch name: `feature/<issue>-<short-name>`.
4. **Always start a branch from the latest `dev`.**
5. **Never commit secrets.** Keys live only in `.env.local`, which is git-ignored.
6. **Don't apply database migrations yourself.** Commit the SQL file; the owner applies it.
7. Run the checks (tests, type check, build) **before** you push for review.

## 2. Branches: what goes where

| Branch | What it is | Who pushes | Deploys to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | Production | Owner only (protected) | https://yulabs-crm-1122.netlify.app |
| `dev` | Integration of everyone's finished work | Merged PRs only | https://dev--yulabs-crm-1122.netlify.app |
| `feature/<issue>-<name>` | Your work on one issue | **You** | nothing (CI runs on the PR) |

```
[your laptop]  feature/4-profile-page
      |
      |  git push -u origin feature/4-profile-page
      v
[GitHub]       feature/4-profile-page
      |
      |  pull request (base: dev) -> CI green -> review -> squash-merge
      v
[GitHub]       dev    -> auto-deploys https://dev--yulabs-crm-1122.netlify.app
      |
      |  owner only: release PR dev -> main
      v
[GitHub]       main   -> auto-deploys https://yulabs-crm-1122.netlify.app
```

**Where you push:** `git push -u origin feature/<issue>-<name>`. That always goes to your own feature branch on `origin`. Then open a PR with **base = `dev`**.

## 3. One-time setup

### 3.1 Install the tools

| Tool | Version | Check |
|---|---|---|
| Git | 2.40+ | `git --version` |
| Node.js | **22** (same as CI) | `node -v` |
| npm | comes with Node | `npm -v` |
| GitHub CLI (optional, recommended) | latest | `gh --version` |
| VS Code (or Cursor) | latest | |
| cloudflared (only for webhook testing) | latest | `cloudflared --version` |

Windows: use **Git Bash** or PowerShell. All commands below work in both unless noted.

### 3.2 Tell Git who you are (once per computer)

```bash
git config --global user.name "Kammar Shashank"
git config --global user.email "<the email on your GitHub account>"
git config --global pull.rebase true
git config --global init.defaultBranch main
```

### 3.3 Sign in to GitHub

```bash
gh auth login          # choose GitHub.com → HTTPS → login with a web browser
gh auth status         # should say: Logged in to github.com account KAMMAR-SHASHANK
```

Without `gh`, Git asks for credentials on your first push. Use the browser sign-in window (Git Credential Manager) or a Personal Access Token, **not** your password.

### 3.4 Clone the repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yulabs-in/CRM-Based-Voice-Agents.git
cd CRM-Based-Voice-Agents
git checkout dev
git pull
```

> Older clones may point at `yulabs-in/screenshot-exact-match`, the repository's old name. GitHub redirects it, but you can update it with `git remote set-url origin https://github.com/yulabs-in/CRM-Based-Voice-Agents.git`.

### 3.5 Install dependencies

```bash
npm ci                 # exact versions from package-lock.json (same as CI)
```

Use `npm ci`, not `npm install`, unless you are adding a package on purpose. If you do add a package (`npm install <pkg>`), commit both `package.json` **and** `package-lock.json`.

### 3.6 Environment variables

```bash
cp .env.example .env.local
```

`.env` (committed) holds the public Supabase values. `.env.local` (git-ignored) holds the server secrets. **Ask the team lead** for the values for `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `SARVAM_API_KEY` and `PUBLIC_APP_URL`. Never paste them into chat, issues, PRs, code or screenshots.

Check that Git ignores the file:

```bash
git check-ignore .env.local      # must print: .env.local
```

### 3.7 Run the app

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open the **Local** URL that Vite prints (for example `http://localhost:8080`). Sign up or sign in, and you should see the dashboard. Stop it with `Ctrl+C`.

### 3.8 Run the tests once, so you know the baseline

```bash
npx vitest run
npx tsc --noEmit       # 10 known errors exist today, so note the number you see
npm run build
```

## 4. Daily development loop

### 4.1 Start an issue

```bash
git checkout dev
git pull                                   # get everyone's latest merged work
git checkout -b feature/4-profile-page       # new branch from dev
```

On GitHub, comment on the issue: "Starting on this today. Branch `feature/4-profile-page`."

### 4.2 Work in small steps

```bash
npm run dev                  # keep it running; the page reloads on save
npx vitest                   # optional: tests in watch mode in a second terminal
```

### 4.3 See what changed

```bash
git status                   # which files changed
git diff                     # the exact lines
```

### 4.4 Commit

```bash
git add src/routes/_authenticated/_app/profile.tsx src/components/app/AppShell.tsx
git commit -m "Profile: upload and remove avatar"
```

- Add files **by name**. Avoid `git add .` unless you've checked `git status` and nothing unexpected (`.env.local`, `dist/`, `.netlify/`, screenshots) is listed.
- One idea per commit; present-tense message under ~70 characters; details in the body if needed.

### 4.5 Push your branch (do this often; it is your backup)

```bash
git push -u origin feature/4-profile-page    # first push: creates the branch on GitHub
git push                                   # later pushes
```

This pushes only to **your feature branch**. It never touches `dev` or `main`.

### 4.6 Stay up to date with `dev` (at least daily, and before opening a PR)

```bash
git fetch origin
git rebase origin/dev        # replay your commits on top of the latest dev
# if there are conflicts: fix the files, then
git add <fixed files>
git rebase --continue
# when the rebase is done, update your remote branch:
git push --force-with-lease
```

`--force-with-lease` is safe on **your own** feature branch, because it refuses to overwrite commits you haven't seen. **Never force-push `dev` or `main`.**

Prefer merging? `git merge origin/dev`, then a normal `git push`. Either is fine; just be consistent within a branch.

## 5. Testing: what to run, and when

### 5.1 Automated checks (every PR, CI runs the first and third too)

```bash
npx vitest run               # all unit tests
npx vitest run src/test/crm-outcome.test.ts    # one file
npx vitest -t "interested"   # tests whose name matches
npx tsc --noEmit             # type check: no NEW errors
npm run build                # production build must succeed
npm run lint                 # lint
```

### 5.2 Writing unit tests

- Put tests in `src/test/<thing>.test.ts`. Vitest with jsdom (see `src/test/crm-outcome.test.ts` for the house style).
- Test **pure functions** first: parsers, rule lookups, permission checks, mappers. Move logic out of components and server routes into small functions so you can test it.
- Freeze time when it matters: `vi.useFakeTimers(); vi.setSystemTime(new Date("2026-11-23T10:00:00+05:30"))`.
- Mock network and Sarvam: `vi.mock("@/lib/sarvam.server", () => ({ ... }))`. Tests must never call real Sarvam or send real messages.

Example:

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { classifyCallOutcome } from "@/lib/crm-outcome";

describe("classifyCallOutcome", () => {
  it("ignores calls that never connected", () => {
    expect(classifyCallOutcome({ status: "no_answer", answers: { disposition: "interested" } })).toBeNull();
  });

  it("qualifies an interested caller", () => {
    const r = classifyCallOutcome({ status: "completed", answers: { disposition: "interested" } });
    expect(r).toMatchObject({ leadStatus: "qualified", dealStage: "qualification" });
  });
});
```

### 5.3 Manual testing checklist

- [ ] The happy path works end to end.
- [ ] Error paths: empty input, bad input, network error. You see friendly messages, not a blank screen.
- [ ] Loading states show (throttle the network in DevTools → Network → "Slow 4G").
- [ ] Desktop width **and** 375 px (DevTools → device toolbar → iPhone SE).
- [ ] Keyboard only: Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Esc.
- [ ] Reload the page: state persisted where it should.
- [ ] **Security:** signed in as a second user in another workspace (use a private window), you cannot see or change the first user's data.
- [ ] Browser console has no new errors or warnings.

### 5.4 Testing webhooks and real calls locally

Sarvam can't reach `localhost`, so open a tunnel:

```bash
cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:<port>
# copy the https://xxxx.trycloudflare.com URL into PUBLIC_APP_URL in .env.local, then restart npm run dev
```

You can also simulate a webhook without placing a call:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:<port>/api/public/sarvam-call-webhook \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @test-payload.json
```

Keep sample payloads out of Git if they contain real data, and **only ever call your own number** with test calls.

### 5.5 Database changes

- Write the SQL in `db/migrations/NNNN_short_name.sql`. NNNN = the highest number on `origin/dev` + 1, checked when you open the PR (`git fetch && git ls-tree --name-only origin/dev db/migrations/ | tail -3`).
- Every table: `organization_id`, RLS on, policies scoped to the user's memberships. Additive changes only.
- Add the new types to `src/integrations/supabase/types.ts` (or ask the lead to regenerate it).
- **Do not run it against Supabase.** In the PR description, say "Migration `00NN_…` needs applying". The owner applies it before merging, while dev and production still share one database.

## 6. Open a pull request into `dev`

### 6.1 Final checks

```bash
git fetch origin && git rebase origin/dev
npx vitest run && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build
git status                   # nothing unexpected; no .env.local, dist/, .netlify/
git push --force-with-lease  # or plain git push if you didn't rebase
```

### 6.2 Create the PR

**With GitHub CLI:**

```bash
gh pr create --base dev --head feature/4-profile-page \
  --title "#4 <issue title>" \
  --body "Closes #4

## What changed
- …

## How I tested
- npx vitest run (all green), npm run build OK
- Manual: …

## Screenshots
(before / after, desktop + 375 px)

## Migration
None | 00NN_name.sql needs applying"
```

**On the website:** open the repo → the yellow banner "feature/… had recent pushes" → **Compare & pull request** → set **base: `dev`** ← compare: your branch → fill in the title and body as above → **Create pull request**.

> Check the base branch: it must say **`dev`**. If it says `main`, change it (Edit next to the title).

Assign yourself, link the issue (`Closes #N` does this), and ask the team lead for review. Open it as a **Draft PR** early if you want feedback before it's finished: `gh pr create --draft …`.

### 6.3 CI and review

- CI runs `npx vitest run` and `npm run build` on every push to the PR. Watch it with `gh pr checks --watch` or in the PR's **Checks** tab.
- If CI is red, open the failed job log, fix the problem locally, commit, and push. The PR updates by itself.
- Review comments: fix them in new commits on the same branch, push, and reply "Done" (or explain) on each comment. Resolve conversations once they're handled.

```bash
gh pr view --web             # open your PR in the browser
gh pr status                 # your PRs and their checks
```

### 6.4 Merge

When CI is green and the PR is approved, the reviewer (or you, if told to) **squash-merges** into `dev`. Delete the branch on GitHub when asked (there's a button).

## 7. After the merge: check the dev preview

1. The push to `dev` triggers **Deploy** (GitHub → Actions). Wait for it to finish (a few minutes).
2. Open https://dev--yulabs-crm-1122.netlify.app and test your feature there, just as you did locally.
3. Comment on the issue: "Merged in #<PR>, verified on the dev preview." The issue closes automatically from `Closes #N`.
4. If something is broken on the preview, open a new small fix branch from `dev` straight away (`feature/<issue>-fix-<what>`).

### 7.1 Clean up locally and start the next issue

```bash
git checkout dev
git pull
git branch -d feature/4-profile-page         # delete the local branch (safe: refuses if unmerged)
git fetch --prune                          # forget branches deleted on GitHub
git checkout -b feature/<next-issue>-<name>
```

After a squash merge, `git branch -d` may say "not fully merged". If the PR shows **Merged**, use `git branch -D …`.

## 8. Fixing common problems

**I committed on `dev` (or `main`) by mistake, and haven't pushed:**

```bash
git branch feature/<issue>-<name>      # keep your commits on a new branch
git reset --hard origin/dev            # put local dev back (on main: origin/main)
git checkout feature/<issue>-<name>
```

**I started coding before creating a branch (nothing committed yet):**

```bash
git checkout -b feature/<issue>-<name>  # your uncommitted changes come with you
```

**Rebase conflict:**

```bash
git status                     # files marked "both modified"
# open each file, keep the right parts, remove <<<<<<< ======= >>>>>>> markers
git add <file>
git rebase --continue
# give up and go back to how it was before:
git rebase --abort
```

For `package-lock.json` conflicts: take dev's version, then reinstall your package:

```bash
git checkout origin/dev -- package-lock.json   # start from dev's lock file
npm install                                     # re-adds your package on top
git add package-lock.json && git rebase --continue
```

**I need to switch tasks with unfinished work:**

```bash
git stash push -m "wip profile"     # put it aside
git checkout other-branch
git checkout -                      # come back
git stash pop
```

**Undo the last commit but keep the changes:** `git reset --soft HEAD~1`

**I committed a secret:** stop. Don't push. If you **already pushed**, tell the team lead **immediately** so the key can be rotated. Removing it from Git history isn't enough once it has been pushed.

**`npm ci` fails:** check `node -v` is 22. Delete `node_modules` and run `npm ci` again.

**Push rejected (`non-fast-forward`):** someone else, or you on another machine, pushed to your branch. Run `git pull --rebase` and then `git push`.

**`Permission denied` / 403 on push:** run `gh auth status`. Make sure you're pushing a `feature/...` branch (not `main`) and that you accepted the repository invitation.

## #4: Profile page

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | https://github.com/yulabs-in/CRM-Based-Voice-Agents/issues/4 |
| **Assignee** | Kammar Shashank (`KAMMAR-SHASHANK`) |
| **Branch** | `feature/4-profile-page` |
| **PR into** | `dev` |
| **Order** | Shashank's 1st issue |
| **Depends on** | nothing |
| **Blocks** | nothing (#25 adds the theme setting to this page later) |
| **Size** | ~3–4 days |

### 1. Summary

Every signed-in user gets a **Profile** page where they can see and edit their own account: photo, name, job title, phone and language. They can also change their password, sign out of other devices, and see which workspaces they belong to. Today the account menu only shows an email initial, and nothing about the user can be changed.

### 2. What already exists

- Migration `db/migrations/0016_profile_details_and_avatars.sql` (applied) adds:
  - `profiles.job_title`, `profiles.phone`, `profiles.preferred_language`
  - a public storage bucket `avatars`; a user may only write inside `avatars/<their user id>/`
- RLS on `profiles`: users may update their own row (`"profiles self update"` in `0000_core_tenancy_crm.sql`).
- `useOrg()` in `src/lib/org.tsx` gives the current workspace and the user's role.
- `src/routes/auth.tsx` has the password **strength meter** and `friendlyError()`; reuse both.
- `src/components/app/AppShell.tsx` renders the account menu (top right).

### 3. Scope

**In scope:** profile page, avatar upload/replace/remove, edit details, change password, sign out of other devices, workspace list, account-menu link and avatar.

**Out of scope:** changing the email address, deleting the account, two-factor auth, theme toggle (that's #25).

### 4. What to build, point by point

#### 4.1 Route and layout
1. Create `src/routes/_authenticated/_app/profile.tsx` with `createFileRoute("/_authenticated/_app/profile")`. The route tree (`src/routeTree.gen.ts`) regenerates when you run `npm run dev`; commit it.
2. Page title "Profile" with `PageHeader`, and a short description ("Your personal details and sign-in").
3. Layout: a single column on mobile; on desktop, the header card across the top with two columns below (Details | Security & workspaces).

#### 4.2 Header card
4. Avatar circle (96 px). It shows the image if `profiles.avatar_url` is set, otherwise the initials from the full name (or the first letter of the email).
5. Next to it: full name (large), email, role badge in the current workspace (`StatusBadge` or `Badge`), and "Member since <Mon YYYY>".
6. Buttons under the avatar: **Upload photo** / **Replace**, and **Remove** (only when there is a photo).

#### 4.3 Avatar upload
7. Hidden `<input type="file" accept="image/png,image/jpeg,image/webp">`.
8. Validate **before uploading**: type is PNG/JPG/WebP and size ≤ 2 MB. Otherwise show the toast "Use a PNG, JPG or WebP image up to 2 MB."
9. Upload path `avatars/<user.id>/avatar-<Date.now()>.<ext>` with `supabase.storage.from("avatars").upload(path, file, { upsert: false, contentType: file.type })`.
10. Get the public URL (`getPublicUrl`) and save it to `profiles.avatar_url`. If the column doesn't exist in `src/integrations/supabase/types.ts`, add migration `00NN_profile_avatar_url.sql`: `alter table public.profiles add column if not exists avatar_url text;`.
11. After saving, delete the **previous** file (if it was in the user's folder).
12. Show an uploading state on the button, and refresh the profile query so the header **and** the account menu update without a reload.
13. **Remove**: delete the file from storage, then set `avatar_url = null`.

#### 4.4 Details form
14. Fields: Full name (required, 2–80 chars), Job title (optional, ≤ 80), Phone (optional, validated with `normalizePhoneNumber`, stored in E.164), Preferred language (select: English, Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati; store codes like `en-IN`, `hi-IN`).
15. Use react-hook-form + zod like the other forms. Show field errors inline.
16. **Save** is disabled until something changes. Show a success toast "Profile saved".
17. Update with `supabase.from("profiles").update({...}).eq("id", user.id)`.

#### 4.5 Security card
18. Change password: New password + Confirm, with the strength meter from `auth.tsx` (extract it into `src/components/app/PasswordStrength.tsx` and use it in both places). Require at least the "fair" level, and require the two fields to match.
19. Call `supabase.auth.updateUser({ password })`, show `friendlyError()` on failure, and clear the fields on success.
20. **Sign out of other devices**: open a confirm dialog, then call `supabase.auth.signOut({ scope: "others" })`, then toast "Signed out everywhere else".

#### 4.6 Workspaces card
21. List every membership: workspace name, role, and a "Current" badge on the active one. Query `memberships` joined with `organizations` for `user_id = auth.uid()`.
22. Optional: a "Switch" button that changes the current workspace with the existing org switcher logic.

#### 4.7 Account menu (`AppShell.tsx`)
23. Add a **Profile** item (icon `User`) linking to `/profile`, above "Sign out".
24. Show the avatar image in the menu trigger, falling back to initials. Use the same profile query, so it updates straight after an upload.

### 5. Data model

No new tables. Only if it's missing:

```sql
-- 00NN_profile_avatar_url.sql: store the public URL of the user's avatar
alter table public.profiles add column if not exists avatar_url text;
```

### 6. Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/routes/_authenticated/_app/profile.tsx` | **new**: the page |
| `src/components/app/PasswordStrength.tsx` | **new**: extracted from `auth.tsx` |
| `src/lib/profile.ts` | **new**: `validateAvatarFile(file)`, `initials(name, email)`, the profile query hook |

| `src/components/app/AppShell.tsx` | Profile menu item and avatar |
| `src/routeTree.gen.ts` | regenerated |
| `src/test/profile.test.ts` | **new** |

### 7. Rules, edge cases, security

- Never trust the client for file checks alone. The bucket policy already restricts the folder; **test it** (below).
- Phone is optional; store `null`, not `""`, when it's empty.
- A long name or email must truncate with an ellipsis, never overflow the card.
- A user with no memberships (just signed up) still sees the page; the workspaces list says "No workspaces yet".
- An upload that fails part-way leaves the old avatar in place.

### 8. Testing

**Unit tests** (`src/test/profile.test.ts`):
- `validateAvatarFile`: accepts PNG/JPG/WebP ≤ 2 MB; rejects GIF, SVG and 2.1 MB files.
- `initials("Kammar Shashank")` → `"KS"`; `initials("", "a@b.com")` → `"A"`; handles extra spaces.

**Manual test script:**
1. Upload a JPG → it appears in the header and the account menu with no reload.
2. Replace it with a PNG → the old file is gone from the bucket (Supabase dashboard → Storage).
3. Remove → initials are shown.
4. Try a 3 MB image and a `.gif` → friendly error, and nothing appears in storage.
5. Edit all fields, save, reload → values persist. Clear the phone → saved as null.
6. Change password → sign out → sign in with the new password.
7. Sign in on a second browser, click "Sign out of other devices" on the first → the second is signed out on its next request.
8. **Security:** signed in as user B, run this in the console:
   `await supabase.storage.from('avatars').upload('<USER_A_ID>/hack.png', new Blob(['x']), { contentType: 'image/png' })` → must return an error.
9. Check at 375 px width, and keyboard only.

```bash

npx vitest run && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build
```

### 9. Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can upload, replace and remove a photo; the header and account menu update without a reload
- [ ] A user can edit full name, job title, phone and language, and the values persist
- [ ] A user can change their password, and sign out of other devices
- [ ] The workspaces list shows every membership and role
- [ ] User B cannot write into user A's avatar folder (tested, noted in the PR)
- [ ] Unit tests added; all checks pass; works at 375 px

## #10: Per-agent outcome rules and lead fields

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | https://github.com/yulabs-in/CRM-Based-Voice-Agents/issues/10 |
| **Assignee** | Kammar Shashank (`KAMMAR-SHASHANK`) |
| **Branch** | `feature/10-agent-outcome-rules` |
| **PR into** | `dev` |
| **Order** | Shashank's 2nd issue |
| **Depends on** | nothing (nicer after #9) |
| **Blocks** | nothing, but #11/#14 (Charan) also edit `crm-sync.server.ts`, so keep your change small |
| **Size** | ~4–5 days |

### 1. Summary

Each voice agent decides how its call outcomes move leads and deals. For example, "interested" on the stock agent might mean deal stage *proposal* at 40%, while on the insurance agent it means *qualification* at 25%. Today one set of rules in code applies to every agent. Also, each agent chooses which of its answers show as columns on the Leads page.

### 2. What already exists

- `classifyCallOutcome(input)` in `src/lib/crm-outcome.ts` returns a `CallVerdict` `{ kind, label, leadStatus, dealStage, probability, score }` from the call's disposition. `nextLeadStatus` / `nextDealStage` never move a record backwards.
- `isDoNotContact(label)`: blocks future calls.
- `applyCallOutcomeToCrm` in `src/lib/crm-sync.server.ts` creates or updates the lead, deal and follow-up task, and handles do-not-contact and escalations.
- Tests: `src/test/crm-outcome.test.ts`, `src/test/crm-rules.test.ts`.
- Leads page: `src/routes/_authenticated/_app/leads.tsx` with `DETAIL_KEYS`, a hard-coded list of answer keys shown as details.

### 3. Scope

**In scope:** the `agent_outcome_rules` table, a settings UI per agent, a rule lookup with fallback in the sync, per-agent lead columns, tests.

**Out of scope:** new dispositions in the Sarvam agents themselves, notifications (#14), meetings (#11).

### 4. What to build, point by point

#### 4.1 Database
1. Migration `00NN_agent_outcome_rules.sql` (§5): the rules table, unique `(agent_id, disposition)`, RLS.
2. Add `voice_agents.lead_columns text[]` (the answer keys shown on Leads for this agent).

#### 4.2 Pure rule logic (`src/lib/outcome-rules.ts`)
3. Type `OutcomeRule = { disposition; lead_status; deal_stage; probability; create_lead; create_task; block_contact }`.
4. `DEFAULT_DISPOSITIONS`: the list the UI shows (`interested`, `consultation_booked`, `callback`, `quote_requested`, `not_interested`, `do_not_contact`, `wrong_number`, `escalated`, `no_answer`).
5. `defaultRuleFor(disposition)`: builds the rule today's `classifyCallOutcome` would produce (call it with a fake completed call), so "Reset to defaults" equals current behaviour.
6. `resolveVerdict(call, rules: OutcomeRule[] | null): CallVerdict | null`:
   - run `classifyCallOutcome(call)` (keeps `null` for non-connected calls)
   - normalise the disposition (lowercase, `_`/`-` → space); if a rule matches, override `leadStatus`, `dealStage`, `probability` and add the flags `createLead`, `createTask`, `blockContact`
   - no rule → return the default verdict unchanged
7. **Keep it pure**: no database access, so it's easy to test.

#### 4.3 Sync (`crm-sync.server.ts`), a small change
8. Load the agent's rules once per call (`select * from agent_outcome_rules where agent_id = call.agent_id`).
9. Replace the direct `classifyCallOutcome` call with `resolveVerdict(call, rules)`.
10. Respect the flags: `create_lead = false` → don't create a lead; `create_task = false` → no follow-up task; `block_contact = true` → run the existing do-not-contact block.
11. Keep `nextLeadStatus` / `nextDealStage` (never move backwards) exactly as they are.

#### 4.4 Settings UI
12. On the Voice Agents page, an **Outcome rules** tab or dialog per agent.
13. One row per disposition: lead status ▾, deal stage ▾ (or "No deal"), probability (0–100), and toggles Create lead / Create task / Block contact.
14. Unsaved rows show the defaults greyed out with a "Default" badge. Editing a row makes it a custom rule.
15. **Save** and **Reset to defaults** (deletes the agent's custom rules, with a confirm dialog).
16. Only owners/admins/voice managers can edit (use `can()` once #16 lands).

#### 4.5 Per-agent lead columns
17. On the same screen: "Show on Leads page", a multi-select of the agent's answer keys (from `answer_variables` in #9, or the distinct keys seen in its calls' `answers`).
18. `leads.tsx`: show the selected keys of the lead's agent as details/columns instead of the hard-coded `DETAIL_KEYS`, falling back to `DETAIL_KEYS` when none are set.

### 5. Data model

```sql
-- 00NN_agent_outcome_rules.sql: per-agent mapping from call disposition to lead/deal changes
create table if not exists public.agent_outcome_rules (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  organization_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id) on delete cascade,
  agent_id uuid not null references public.voice_agents(id) on delete cascade,
  disposition text not null,
  lead_status text,
  deal_stage text,
  probability int check (probability between 0 and 100),
  create_lead boolean not null default true,
  create_task boolean not null default true,
  block_contact boolean not null default false,
  updated_by uuid default auth.uid(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (agent_id, disposition)
);
alter table public.agent_outcome_rules enable row level security;
create policy "tenant read" on public.agent_outcome_rules for select to authenticated using (public.is_org_member(organization_id));
create policy "admins write" on public.agent_outcome_rules for all to authenticated
  using (public.has_org_role(organization_id, array['owner','admin','voice_manager']::public.org_role[]))
  with check (public.has_org_role(organization_id, array['owner','admin','voice_manager']::public.org_role[]));
grant select, insert, update, delete on public.agent_outcome_rules to authenticated;
grant all on public.agent_outcome_rules to service_role;

alter table public.voice_agents add column if not exists lead_columns text[] not null default '{}';
```

### 6. Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `db/migrations/00NN_agent_outcome_rules.sql` | **new** |
| `src/lib/outcome-rules.ts` | **new**: pure logic |
| `src/lib/crm-sync.server.ts` | use `resolveVerdict` and the flags (small diff) |
| `src/components/app/agents/OutcomeRules.tsx` | **new**: settings UI |
| `src/routes/_authenticated/_app/voice-agents.tsx` | open the rules UI |
| `src/routes/_authenticated/_app/leads.tsx` | per-agent columns |
| `src/test/outcome-rules.test.ts` | **new** |

### 7. Rules and edge cases

- With **no custom rules**, behaviour must be **identical** to today (all existing tests pass unchanged).
- A disposition with no rule → default. An unknown disposition → default classification.
- Never move a lead or deal backwards (keep `nextLeadStatus`/`nextDealStage`).
- `block_contact` only ever adds a block. Unblocking is done on the DNC page (#13).
- Calls without `agent_id` (old data) → defaults.

### 8. Testing

**Unit tests** (`src/test/outcome-rules.test.ts`):
- no rules → `resolveVerdict` equals `classifyCallOutcome` for every disposition in `DEFAULT_DISPOSITIONS`
- a rule overrides stage and probability for its agent
- agent A's rule doesn't affect agent B (pass B's empty rules)
- `create_lead=false` and `block_contact=true` flags come through
- a non-connected call → `null`, even with rules

**Manual:**
1. For the stock agent, set "interested → proposal, 40%".
2. Simulate a completed webhook with `disposition: interested` for the stock agent and for the insurance agent (see the webhook test steps in your guide, §5.4).
3. Stock deal → proposal 40%; insurance deal → qualification (default).
4. Reset to defaults → behaviour is back to normal.
5. Choose lead columns for the stock agent → the Leads page shows them for stock leads only.

```bash
npx vitest run src/test/outcome-rules.test.ts src/test/crm-outcome.test.ts src/test/crm-rules.test.ts
npx vitest run && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build
```

### 9. Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rules can be edited per agent and reset to defaults
- [ ] Changing a rule for one agent changes only that agent's leads and deals
- [ ] With no rules, behaviour is unchanged (existing tests pass)
- [ ] New tests for rule lookup and fallback
- [ ] The Leads page shows each agent's chosen answer columns

```bash
git checkout dev && git pull
git checkout -b feature/10-agent-outcome-rules
git add src/lib/outcome-rules.ts src/test/outcome-rules.test.ts
git commit -m "Outcome rules: pure resolver with defaults and tests"
git push -u origin feature/10-agent-outcome-rules
git fetch origin && git rebase origin/dev && git push --force-with-lease
gh pr create --base dev --title "#10 Per-agent outcome rules and lead fields" --body "Closes #10 ..."
```

- `Closes #10`; the migration to apply
- A table: disposition → default vs the example custom rule; screenshots of the UI

## #16: Roles and feature access for users

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | https://github.com/yulabs-in/CRM-Based-Voice-Agents/issues/16 |
| **Assignee** | Kammar Shashank (`KAMMAR-SHASHANK`) |
| **Branch** | `feature/16-roles-access` |
| **PR into** | `dev` |
| **Order** | Shashank's 3rd issue (land it early: others use it) |
| **Depends on** | nothing |
| **Used by** | #5 API-key screen, #23 costs (Charan), #9 agent management (Tejaswini), #10 rules (you) |
| **Size** | ~5–6 days |

### 1. Summary

Admins decide which users can use which features. One **permission map** says what each role can do; admins can grant or remove single features per user; the UI hides what a user can't use, **and the server refuses it too**. Every change is audited.

### 2. What already exists

- `memberships.role` (enum `public.org_role`): `owner`, `admin`, `sales_manager`, `sales_rep`, `voice_manager`, `support_agent`, `read_only`.
- SQL helpers: `public.is_org_member(org)`, `public.has_org_role(org, roles[])`, `public.can_write_org(org)`.
- Role checks scattered in server functions (search for `role` / `has_org_role` / `"owner"` in `src/lib/*.functions.ts`).
- Team page: `src/routes/_authenticated/_app/team.tsx`; `useOrg()` returns the current role.

### 3. Scope

**In scope:** the permission map, per-user overrides, a `can()` helper for client and server, the team page role/override editor, nav/button hiding, server enforcement in existing server functions, RLS where it matters, an audit log.

**Out of scope:** custom roles created by admins (note it as a follow-up), field-level permissions.

### 4. What to build, point by point

#### 4.1 Permission map (`src/lib/permissions.ts`), shared by client and server
1. Features (string union):
   `calls.place`, `campaigns.run`, `agents.manage`, `recordings.view`, `transcripts.view`, `data.export`, `contacts.edit`, `contacts.delete`, `api_keys.manage`, `settings.manage`, `team.manage`, `billing.view`, `dnc.manage`.
2. `ROLE_PERMISSIONS: Record<OrgRole, Feature[]>`, for example:

| Feature | owner | admin | sales_manager | sales_rep | voice_manager | support_agent | read_only |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| calls.place | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | |
| campaigns.run | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | ✓ | | |
| agents.manage | ✓ | ✓ | | | ✓ | | |
| recordings.view | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | |
| data.export | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | | | |
| api_keys.manage | ✓ | ✓ | | | | | |
| settings.manage | ✓ | ✓ | | | | | |
| team.manage | ✓ | ✓ | | | | | |
| billing.view | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | | | |
| dnc.manage | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | | ✓ | |

   (Agree the final table with the lead; put it in the PR.)
3. `can(role, feature, overrides?: { grant: Feature[]; revoke: Feature[] }): boolean`. Owners can always do everything (revokes don't apply to owners).
4. A React hook `useCan(feature)` built on `useOrg()` plus the user's overrides.
5. A `<Can feature="agents.manage">…</Can>` component for hiding UI.

#### 4.2 Server enforcement
6. `requirePermission(context, orgId, feature)` in `src/lib/permissions.server.ts`: loads the membership and overrides, and throws a 403-style error "You don't have access to manage agents."
7. Add it at the top of every sensitive server function: agent create/edit/publish, campaign launch, exports, API keys, settings, team changes, DNC reactivation.
8. Where the database is written directly from the client (RLS), add policies for the most sensitive tables (e.g. `voice_agents` write needs `owner/admin/voice_manager`), using a SQL function `public.has_feature(org, feature)` that mirrors the map. **Keep the SQL map and the TS map in sync**; a unit test compares them (export the TS map to a JSON fixture that the migration comment references).

#### 4.3 Team page
9. Members table: name, email, role ▾ (owners/admins only), "Custom access" badge if there are overrides, last active.
10. A "Customise access" drawer: a checkbox per feature showing the role default; ticking or unticking creates a grant or revoke override. "Reset to role defaults".
11. Rules: you can't demote the last owner; you can't change your own role; only owners can make owners.

#### 4.4 Hide in the UI
12. Sidebar (`AppShell.tsx`): hide nav items whose feature the user lacks (Voice Agents edit, Settings, Team, API keys, exports).
13. Buttons: Launch campaign, Export CSV, Edit agent, Delete contact, Revoke key: wrap in `<Can>`.
14. Direct URL to a forbidden page → show "You don't have access to this page", plus a link back (don't crash).

#### 4.5 Audit
15. A `role_audit` table: who changed whose role/overrides, from → to, when. Show it at the bottom of the Team page (admins).

### 5. Data model

```sql
-- 00NN_roles_access.sql: per-user permission overrides, audit of role changes, and has_feature() for RLS
create table if not exists public.membership_permission_overrides (
  organization_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id) on delete cascade,
  user_id uuid not null references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
  feature text not null,
  granted boolean not null,            -- true = grant, false = revoke
  updated_by uuid default auth.uid(), updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  primary key (organization_id, user_id, feature)
);
create table if not exists public.role_audit (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  organization_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id) on delete cascade,
  actor uuid default auth.uid(), target_user uuid not null,
  change jsonb not null,               -- {"role":{"from":"sales_rep","to":"sales_manager"}} or {"grant":"agents.manage"}
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
-- RLS: members read overrides of their org; only owners/admins write overrides and read the audit.
-- create or replace function public.has_feature(_org uuid, _feature text) returns boolean ... security definer ...
```

### 6. Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `db/migrations/00NN_roles_access.sql` | **new** |
| `src/lib/permissions.ts` | **new**: map, `can`, `useCan`, `<Can>` |
| `src/lib/permissions.server.ts` | **new**: `requirePermission` |
| `src/lib/*.functions.ts` | add `requirePermission` calls |
| `src/routes/_authenticated/_app/team.tsx` | role editor, overrides, audit |
| `src/components/app/AppShell.tsx` | hide nav items |
| `src/components/app/NoAccess.tsx` | **new** |
| `src/test/permissions.test.ts` | **new** |

### 7. Rules, edge cases, security

- **Hiding is not security.** Every hidden action must also be refused by the server (and RLS where the client writes directly).
- Last-owner protection; no self-demotion; only owners create owners.
- Overrides survive a role change (or are cleared; decide and document it).
- Role changes take effect on the user's next request (refetch the membership on focus).

### 8. Testing

**Unit tests:** `can()` for every role × feature against the table; overrides grant/revoke; owners ignore revokes; last-owner protection logic; the TS map equals the SQL map fixture.

**Manual test script:**
1. Create a test user as `sales_rep` in your workspace (invite flow).
2. As the rep: no Voice Agents edit, Settings, Team or API keys in the nav; opening `/settings` directly shows "No access".
3. As the rep, replay an agent-update server function request (DevTools → Network → copy as fetch → run in the console) → refused.
4. As admin: grant the rep `agents.manage` → the rep can now edit agents (after a refresh).
5. The audit shows both changes.
6. Try to demote the only owner → blocked.

```bash
npx vitest run src/test/permissions.test.ts
npx vitest run && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build
```

### 9. Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A sales rep can't open agent management or API-key screens: both the UI and the server refuse
- [ ] An admin can grant access per user, and it works
- [ ] One permission map is used by client and server; role changes are audited
- [ ] Last-owner and self-demotion protections work

### 10. Git workflow for this issue

```bash
git checkout dev && git pull
git checkout -b feature/16-roles-access
git add src/lib/permissions.ts src/test/permissions.test.ts
git commit -m "Roles: permission map and can() helper"
git push -u origin feature/16-roles-access
git fetch origin && git rebase origin/dev && git push --force-with-lease
gh pr create --base dev --title "#16 Roles and feature access" --body "Closes #16 ..."
```

### 11. In the pull request

- `Closes #16`; the migration to apply
- The final role × feature table; the list of server functions now protected
- A note for teammates: "Use `requirePermission(ctx, org, 'api_keys.manage')` / `<Can feature=…>`"

### 12. Settle with the lead before starting

- The final role × feature table.
- Whether overrides are kept or cleared on a role change.

## #13: Do-not-contact registry and compliance log

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | https://github.com/yulabs-in/CRM-Based-Voice-Agents/issues/13 |
| **Assignee** | Kammar Shashank (`KAMMAR-SHASHANK`) |
| **Branch** | `feature/13-dnc-registry` |
| **PR into** | `dev` |
| **Order** | Shashank's 4th issue |
| **Depends on** | nothing |
| **Used by** | #5 `POST /api/v1/calls` and #20 widget (Charan), #12 WhatsApp (Tejaswini), #19 inbound (you) |
| **Size** | ~5 days |

### 1. Summary

Never call someone who opted out, and be able to **prove** it. Blocking moves from the contact record to the **phone number**, so a number stays blocked even when it's re-imported as a new contact. Every consent, opt-out, block and reactivation is written to a compliance log that can be exported.

### 2. What already exists

- When a caller says "do not contact / do not call / opt out", `applyCallOutcomeToCrm` sets the contact to `status = 'inactive'` and adds the tag `do-not-call` (`isDoNotContact()` in `src/lib/crm-outcome.ts`).
- Campaigns skip inactive contacts. `startSarvamCall` refuses numbers belonging to inactive contacts (a `phoneKey()` comparison in `src/lib/sarvam.functions.ts`).
- `normalizePhoneNumber` exists for E.164.

### 3. Scope

**In scope:** `dnc_numbers` and `compliance_log` tables, one `isBlocked()` helper used everywhere, recording blocks from calls, the Do-not-contact page (list/search/add/reactivate), CSV export, a backfill of existing blocked contacts.

**Optional:** importing a national DND list.

### 4. What to build, point by point

#### 4.1 Database
1. Migration `00NN_dnc_registry.sql` (§5): `dnc_numbers` and `compliance_log`, RLS, and a **backfill** that inserts the phone of every existing contact with `status = 'inactive'` and tag `do-not-call`.

#### 4.2 Helper (`src/lib/dnc.server.ts`)
2. `toE164(phone)`: wraps `normalizePhoneNumber`. `+91 98480 12345`, `09848012345`, `9848012345` and `+919848012345` all become `+919848012345`.
3. `isBlocked(orgId, phone): Promise<boolean>`: an active row (`removed_at is null`) exists.
4. `blockNumber({ orgId, phone, reason, source, callId?, actor? })`: upsert into `dnc_numbers` and write a `compliance_log` row (`event = 'opt_out'` from a call, or `'blocked'` manual/import).
5. `unblockNumber({ orgId, phone, reason, actor })`: requires a reason (min 10 chars); sets `removed_at/by/reason` and logs `reactivated`. Also set matching contacts back to `active` and remove the tag.
6. `logBlockedAttempt({ orgId, phone, where })`: logs `blocked_attempt` whenever a call was refused.

#### 4.3 Use the registry everywhere
7. `crm-sync.server.ts`: when `isDoNotContact(...)`, also call `blockNumber(... source: 'call', callId)`. Keep the existing contact update.
8. `startSarvamCall` (one-off calls): replace or extend the inactive-contact check with `isBlocked()`. Refuse with the existing message, and call `logBlockedAttempt`.
9. Campaign launch / target building: exclude blocked numbers, and mark those targets `skipped` with reason `do_not_contact`.
10. Consent: when an answer says consent was given (`consent_to_share = yes`), log `consent_given` with the call id.
11. Export `isBlocked` for Charan (#5, #20) and Tejaswini (#12). Mention it in the PR.

#### 4.4 Do-not-contact page
12. Route `src/routes/_authenticated/_app/do-not-contact.tsx`, linked in the sidebar under Calls or Settings.
13. Table: number (masked except the last 4 digits for non-admins), contact name (if any), reason, source (Call/Manual/Import), blocked at, blocked by / call link. Search by number or name, and filter by source.
14. **Add number** dialog: phone (validated) and reason.
15. **Reactivate** dialog: a required reason, and a warning "Only reactivate if the person has asked to be contacted."
16. **Compliance log** tab: events with time, actor, number, call link and details; filter by event and date; **Export CSV**.
17. Optional: **Import DND list** (CSV with one number per line). Stream in batches of 500 with a progress bar.

### 5. Data model

```sql
-- 00NN_dnc_registry.sql: phone-level do-not-contact registry and compliance audit log
create table if not exists public.dnc_numbers (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  organization_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id) on delete cascade,
  phone_e164 text not null,
  reason text, source text not null default 'manual' check (source in ('call','manual','import')),
  call_id uuid references public.calls(id) on delete set null,
  created_by uuid default auth.uid(), created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  removed_at timestamptz, removed_by uuid, removed_reason text
);
create unique index if not exists dnc_numbers_active_key on public.dnc_numbers (organization_id, phone_e164) where removed_at is null;

create table if not exists public.compliance_log (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  organization_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id) on delete cascade,
  phone_e164 text, contact_id uuid references public.contacts(id) on delete set null,
  event text not null check (event in ('consent_given','opt_out','blocked','reactivated','blocked_attempt')),
  actor uuid, call_id uuid references public.calls(id) on delete set null,
  details jsonb not null default '{}', created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index if not exists compliance_log_org_time_idx on public.compliance_log (organization_id, created_at desc);
-- RLS: members read both; inserts into compliance_log only via the service role (no insert policy for authenticated,
-- so the log can't be forged from the browser); dnc_numbers writes for can_write_org.

-- Backfill from existing blocked contacts (adapt the phone normalisation to what the contacts table stores)
insert into public.dnc_numbers (organization_id, phone_e164, reason, source)
select distinct organization_id, phone, 'Backfilled from do-not-call contacts', 'call'
from public.contacts where status = 'inactive' and 'do-not-call' = any(tags) and phone is not null
on conflict do nothing;
```

### 6. Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `db/migrations/00NN_dnc_registry.sql` | **new** |
| `src/lib/dnc.server.ts` | **new**: helpers |
| `src/lib/dnc.functions.ts` | **new**: list/add/reactivate/export server functions |
| `src/lib/crm-sync.server.ts`, `src/lib/sarvam.functions.ts`, campaign launch code | use the registry |
| `src/routes/_authenticated/_app/do-not-contact.tsx` | **new** |
| `src/components/app/AppShell.tsx` | nav link |
| `src/test/dnc.test.ts` | **new** |

### 7. Rules, edge cases, security

- The compliance log is **append-only**: no update or delete from the app.
- Reactivation always needs a reason and is always logged.
- An inbound caller (#19) on the DNC list may still call in, but **no outbound follow-ups** are scheduled.
- Normalise every number before comparing, so different spellings of the same number never get past the block.
- Only members of the org can see its registry.

### 8. Testing

**Unit tests:** `toE164` for every format above; `isBlocked` true/false and after a removal; `unblockNumber` without a reason throws; the campaign target filter excludes blocked numbers.

**Manual test script:**
1. Add `+91 90000 00001` manually → listed; the log shows `blocked`.
2. Import a CSV project containing `09000000001` as a new contact → run a campaign → that target is **skipped** (reason `do_not_contact`).
3. Test call to that number → refused; the log shows `blocked_attempt`.
4. Simulate a webhook where a caller says "do not call me" → the number is in the registry with a link to the call.
5. Reactivate it with a reason → the contact is active again; the log shows `reactivated` with your name.
6. Export CSV → it opens in Excel with every event.

```bash
npx vitest run src/test/dnc.test.ts
npx vitest run && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build
```

### 9. Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An imported contact with a blocked number is skipped by a campaign
- [ ] One-off calls (and the API in #5) refuse blocked numbers
- [ ] The log shows when, how and by whom a number was blocked or reactivated; CSV export works
- [ ] Existing do-not-call contacts are backfilled
- [ ] The `isBlocked()` helper is documented for other issues

## #19: Inbound calls: the agent answers your business number

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | https://github.com/yulabs-in/CRM-Based-Voice-Agents/issues/19 |
| **Assignee** | Kammar Shashank (`KAMMAR-SHASHANK`) |
| **Branch** | `feature/19-inbound-calls` |
| **PR into** | `dev` |
| **Order** | Shashank's 5th issue |
| **Depends on** | #13 (DNC: no outbound follow-ups for opted-out callers) |
| **Blocks** | nothing |
| **Size** | ~5–6 days |

### 1. Summary

When a customer **calls the business number**, a voice agent answers. The call lands in the CRM exactly like an outbound one: a call row (`direction = inbound`), contact found or created by phone, answers/transcript/recording saved, and leads, deals and tasks updated by the same CRM sync.

### 2. What already exists

- `calls.direction` already exists (default `'outbound'`).
- The outbound result webhook `src/routes/api/public/sarvam-call-webhook.ts`: verifies the token, extracts answers (`extractAnswers`), saves the transcript and recording, then `applyCallOutcomeToCrm(call)`.
- `crm-sync.server.ts`: `applyCallOutcomeToCrm`.
- Live Calls / Call History pages: `live-calls.tsx`, `call-history.tsx`.
- Sarvam: inbound deployments link an agent + telephony connection + number (see the Sarvam docs: telephony, deployments).

### 3. Scope

**In scope:** managing the inbound deployment from Voice Agents (which agent answers, business hours), an inbound webhook route, contact match/create, the same sync, the "Inbound" badge and a direction filter, the DNC follow-up rule.

**Out of scope:** call transfer to a human, IVR menus, voicemail transcription (unless Sarvam provides it for free).

### 4. What to build, point by point

#### 4.1 Inbound settings (Voice Agents page)
1. An "Inbound" section: business number (from the telephony connection), the agent that answers ▾, business hours (days, start/end, timezone Asia/Kolkata), and an out-of-hours behaviour (another agent ▾, or "Sarvam default message").
2. Saving calls Sarvam (server function) to create or update the inbound deployment for that number. Store the deployment id.
3. A status chip: "Live: calls to +91 … are answered by <agent>".

#### 4.2 Inbound webhook (`src/routes/api/public/sarvam-inbound-webhook.ts`)
4. Verify the request: a secret token in the URL path or header, compared by SHA-256 (like `cron-sync.ts`). Reject anything else with 401.
5. Map the payload: caller number (`from`), our number (`to`), Sarvam call id, status, duration, `final_agent_variables`, transcript, recording URL.
6. Find the organization by the called number (the deployment → org mapping saved in 4.1).
7. **Idempotent:** upsert the call by `external_id` (the Sarvam call id). Repeated events update the same row.
8. Find the contact by **normalised phone** in that org; if there's none, create one (`first_name` from the spoken name answer if any, otherwise "Inbound caller", source tag `inbound`).
9. Insert or update `calls` with `direction = 'inbound'`, `agent_id`, `contact_id`, status, timings, answers, transcript, recording (reuse the helpers from the outbound webhook; move them into `src/lib/call-ingest.server.ts` so both routes share them).
10. When completed, run `applyCallOutcomeToCrm(call)` (same lead/deal/task logic).
11. If the inbound call is still live (in progress), make sure Live Calls shows it (Realtime already covers `calls`).

#### 4.3 DNC rule
12. If the caller's number is blocked (`isBlocked()` from #13), still record the call, but **don't create outbound follow-up tasks or calls**: pass a flag `suppressFollowUps: true` to the sync, which skips follow-up task creation and campaign enrolment.

#### 4.4 UI
13. Call History and Live Calls: an **Inbound** badge (icon `PhoneIncoming`) vs Outbound, and a direction filter (All / Outbound / Inbound).
14. Contact timeline: "Called in" wording for inbound calls.

### 5. Data model

```sql
-- 00NN_inbound_calls.sql: inbound deployments (which agent answers which number) and a secret for the inbound webhook
create table if not exists public.inbound_deployments (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  organization_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id) on delete cascade,
  phone_number text not null unique,               -- E.164 business number
  agent_id uuid references public.voice_agents(id) on delete set null,
  after_hours_agent_id uuid references public.voice_agents(id) on delete set null,
  business_hours jsonb not null default '{"days":["Monday","Tuesday","Wednesday","Thursday","Friday","Saturday"],"start":"09:00","end":"19:00","tz":"Asia/Kolkata"}',
  sarvam_deployment_id text,
  webhook_token_hash text,
  active boolean not null default true,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(), updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
create unique index if not exists calls_external_id_key on public.calls (organization_id, external_id) where external_id is not null;
-- RLS: members read; owners/admins/voice_managers write (has_org_role)
```

Check that no existing duplicate `external_id` values block the unique index. Run a `select external_id, count(*) … having count(*) > 1` first and mention the result in the PR.

### 6. Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `db/migrations/00NN_inbound_calls.sql` | **new** |
| `src/lib/call-ingest.server.ts` | **new**: shared mapping/saving helpers (moved from the outbound webhook) |
| `src/routes/api/public/sarvam-inbound-webhook.ts` | **new** |
| `src/routes/api/public/sarvam-call-webhook.ts` | use the shared helpers (no behaviour change) |
| `src/lib/inbound.functions.ts` | **new**: save the deployment via Sarvam |
| `src/lib/crm-sync.server.ts` | `suppressFollowUps` option |
| `voice-agents.tsx`, `call-history.tsx`, `live-calls.tsx` | UI |
| `src/test/inbound.test.ts` | **new** |

### 7. Rules, edge cases, security

- The webhook must be authenticated (token) and idempotent (upsert by `external_id`).
- Withheld or unknown caller id → create the call without a contact; don't crash.
- Out of business hours → the after-hours agent or the default message (configured in Sarvam).
- Refactoring the outbound webhook must not change its behaviour. The existing tests must still pass (`src/test/sarvam-call.test.ts`).
- Blocked callers: the call is logged, follow-ups are suppressed.

### 8. Testing

**Unit tests:** payload → call row mapping; contact match with different phone formats; a new contact for an unknown number; a repeated event updates rather than duplicates; `suppressFollowUps` skips task creation.

**Manual:**
1. Start a tunnel: `cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8080` → set `PUBLIC_APP_URL` → restart `npm run dev`.
2. Configure inbound for the test number with the insurance agent.
3. Call the test number **from your own phone**, and say you're interested.
4. Within seconds: Live Calls shows it with the Inbound badge → after hanging up, Call History has it with the transcript; the contact exists (or was created); the lead appears under Interested.
5. Block your number (#13), call again → the call is recorded, and no follow-up task is created.
6. Simulate the webhook with curl and a saved payload, twice → one call row.

```bash
npx vitest run src/test/inbound.test.ts src/test/sarvam-call.test.ts
npx vitest run && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build
```

### 9. Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Calling the test number reaches the chosen agent
- [ ] The call, contact and (if interested) lead appear in the CRM within seconds
- [ ] Inbound calls are badged and filterable; the webhook is authenticated and idempotent
- [ ] Opted-out callers get no outbound follow-ups
- [ ] The outbound webhook still behaves the same (tests pass)

### 10. Git workflow for this issue

```bash
git checkout dev && git pull            # #13 merged first
git checkout -b feature/19-inbound-calls
git add src/lib/call-ingest.server.ts src/routes/api/public/sarvam-inbound-webhook.ts
git commit -m "Inbound: webhook with contact match and CRM sync"
git push -u origin feature/19-inbound-calls
git fetch origin && git rebase origin/dev && git push --force-with-lease
gh pr create --base dev --title "#19 Inbound calls" --body "Closes #19 ..."
```

### 11. In the pull request

- `Closes #19`; the migration to apply (and the duplicate `external_id` check result)
- A recording or screenshots of an inbound test call appearing live

### 12. Settle with the lead before starting

- Which test number and connection to use, and Sarvam's inbound payload format.
- Business hours and the after-hours behaviour.

## #22: AI contact summary and next best action

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | https://github.com/yulabs-in/CRM-Based-Voice-Agents/issues/22 |
| **Assignee** | Kammar Shashank (`KAMMAR-SHASHANK`) |
| **Branch** | `feature/22-ai-contact-summary` |
| **PR into** | `dev` |
| **Order** | Shashank's 6th issue |
| **Depends on** | nothing (needs an LLM API key from the lead) |
| **Blocks** | nothing |
| **Size** | ~4–5 days |

### 1. Summary

Open a contact and **immediately understand where things stand and what to do next**. An AI-generated card shows a 3-line summary of the relationship, the sentiment trend, and **one** recommended next action with a reason. It's built only from data the CRM already has, cached, and refreshed when a new call comes in.

### 2. What already exists

- Per contact: `calls` (summary, answers, sentiment, outcome, dates), `deals` (stage, value), `tasks`, `meetings`.
- `applyCallOutcomeToCrm` in `src/lib/crm-sync.server.ts` runs after every completed call: the hook for refreshing.
- Contact page/drawer (`contacts.tsx` / `EntityPage`), Leads rows (`leads.tsx`).

### 3. Scope

**In scope:** the server function that builds the prompt and calls the LLM, structured JSON output, the `contact_insights` cache, refresh on a new call, the contact card, the lead-row hover card, a manual refresh button, the "AI-generated" label.

**Out of scope:** chat with the contact's history, automatic actions (the AI only *recommends*).

### 4. What to build, point by point

#### 4.1 Provider
1. Agree on the LLM provider and model with the lead (e.g. Claude Haiku for speed and cost). The key goes in `.env.local` / Netlify env (e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), server-side only.
2. A thin client `src/lib/llm.server.ts`: `generateJson<T>(system, user, schema): Promise<T>` with a timeout (15 s), one retry, and zod validation of the output.

#### 4.2 Building the input (`src/lib/insights.server.ts`)
3. `collectContactContext(orgId, contactId)`: the last 10 calls (date, agent, outcome/disposition, sentiment, summary, objections, follow-up time), open deals (stage, value, updated), open tasks (title, due), upcoming meetings, and the contact's status/tags (e.g. do-not-call).
4. Keep it compact: trim summaries to ~400 chars and drop transcripts. Include **no data the CRM doesn't hold**, and don't add the email or full phone (not needed).
5. Prompt (system): *"You are a CRM assistant. Use ONLY the facts provided. If information is missing, say so. Never invent dates, amounts or promises. If the contact asked not to be contacted, the next action must respect that. Reply in JSON matching the schema."*
6. Output schema (zod):
   `{ summary: string (≤ 3 short sentences), sentiment: "improving" | "steady" | "declining" | "unknown", next_action: { action: string (≤ 12 words), reason: string (≤ 30 words), due: "today" | "this_week" | "later" | null }, confidence: "high" | "medium" | "low" }`
7. **Guardrails in code** (don't rely only on the prompt): if the contact is do-not-call → force `next_action = { action: "Do not contact", reason: "Contact opted out" }`. With no calls → no LLM call at all; show "Not enough history yet".

#### 4.3 Cache and refresh
8. Table `contact_insights` (§5): one row per contact, with `source_hash` (a hash of the input context) and `generated_at`.
9. `getContactInsight(contactId)` (server function): if a cached row exists and its `source_hash` matches the current context → return it; otherwise generate, upsert and return.
10. Refresh on a new call: at the end of `applyCallOutcomeToCrm`, call `refreshContactInsight(contactId)` **without awaiting** in the request path (fire-and-forget with catch), so call processing isn't slowed down or broken by LLM errors.
11. Rate-limit generation per org (e.g. 60/hour) to control cost.

#### 4.4 UI
12. A contact page card "AI summary": the summary, a sentiment chip (with an arrow icon), the next action in bold with its reason, "Updated 3 min ago", a **Refresh** button, and an **"AI-generated: check before acting"** label.
13. Leads page: a hover card (or popover on mobile) on the contact name with a compact version.
14. Loading skeleton; on error: "Couldn't generate a summary" + Retry (never block the page).

### 5. Data model

```sql
-- 00NN_contact_insights.sql: cached AI summary per contact
create table if not exists public.contact_insights (
  contact_id uuid primary key references public.contacts(id) on delete cascade,
  organization_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id) on delete cascade,
  summary text not null, sentiment text not null,
  next_action jsonb not null, confidence text,
  source_hash text not null, source_call_ids uuid[] not null default '{}',
  model text, generated_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
alter table public.contact_insights enable row level security;
create policy "tenant read" on public.contact_insights for select to authenticated using (public.is_org_member(organization_id));
grant select on public.contact_insights to authenticated;
grant all on public.contact_insights to service_role;   -- written by the server only
```

### 6. Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `db/migrations/00NN_contact_insights.sql` | **new** |
| `src/lib/llm.server.ts` | **new** |
| `src/lib/insights.server.ts` | **new**: context, prompt, guardrails, cache |
| `src/lib/insights.functions.ts` | **new**: `getContactInsight`, `refreshContactInsight` |
| `src/lib/crm-sync.server.ts` | fire-and-forget refresh |
| `src/components/app/ContactInsightCard.tsx` | **new** |
| contact page, `leads.tsx` | show the card / hover |
| `src/test/insights.test.ts` | **new** |

### 7. Rules, edge cases, security

- **Never invent facts.** The prompt plus guardrails, and confidence shown as "low" when the data is thin.
- The API key stays server-side; never log prompts containing personal data in production.
- LLM down or slow → the CRM keeps working; the card shows an error with Retry.
- Opted-out contacts → "Do not contact" is always the next action.
- Cost control: cache by `source_hash`, and rate-limit per org.

### 8. Testing

**Unit tests (mock the LLM):**
- `collectContactContext` trims and orders data, and excludes transcripts
- the prompt builder includes the facts and the rules
- the output parser rejects invalid JSON or schema (and the retry works)
- the do-not-call guardrail overrides the LLM's suggestion
- no calls → no LLM call
- the same context → cache hit (no LLM call); a new call → a new hash → regenerated

**Manual:**
1. A contact with 3+ calls → the card summary matches the call history (read the calls and compare).
2. Simulate a new completed call → the card updates within a minute (reload or wait for refetch).
3. A do-not-call contact → "Do not contact".
4. Set a wrong API key → the page still works; the card shows an error.

```bash
npx vitest run src/test/insights.test.ts
npx vitest run && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build
```

### 9. Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For a contact with several calls, the card's summary matches the call history
- [ ] It refreshes within a minute of a new call
- [ ] It's clearly labelled AI-generated and never invents facts (guardrails tested)
- [ ] Cached; LLM failures never break the page or the call sync

### 10. Git workflow for this issue

```bash
git checkout dev && git pull
git checkout -b feature/22-ai-contact-summary
git add db/migrations/00NN_contact_insights.sql src/lib/insights.server.ts src/lib/llm.server.ts
git commit -m "Insights: contact context, prompt and cached summary"
git push -u origin feature/22-ai-contact-summary
git fetch origin && git rebase origin/dev && git push --force-with-lease
gh pr create --base dev --title "#22 AI contact summary and next best action" --body "Closes #22 ..."
```

### 11. In the pull request

- `Closes #22`; the migration to apply; the env var name for the LLM key (no value)
- 2–3 example cards next to the real call history they came from

### 12. Settle with the lead before starting

- The LLM provider/model, the key, and a monthly budget.
- Whether the hover card on Leads is needed in v1.

## #25: Dark mode and installable mobile app (PWA)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | https://github.com/yulabs-in/CRM-Based-Voice-Agents/issues/25 |
| **Assignee** | Kammar Shashank (`KAMMAR-SHASHANK`) |
| **Branch** | `feature/25-dark-mode-pwa` (or two: `feature/25-dark-mode`, `feature/25-pwa`) |
| **PR into** | `dev` |
| **Order** | Shashank's 7th issue |
| **Depends on** | nothing; agree on colours with Charan (#8 UI polish); the theme setting fits on the #4 Profile page |
| **Blocks** | nothing |
| **Size** | ~5–6 days |

### 1. Summary

The app is **comfortable at night** (dark theme with a System / Light / Dark toggle, saved per user, no flash on load) and **usable as an app on a phone** (installable PWA with a manifest, icons, an offline-friendly shell and an install prompt; Live Calls and Leads work at phone width).

### 2. What already exists

- Design tokens as CSS variables in `src/styles.css` (Tailwind v4, shadcn). The `.dark` variant may be partly defined; check it.
- Utilities `bg-gradient-primary`, `shadow-soft`, `shadow-float`, `dot-canvas`.
- Charts with Recharts (some hard-coded colours, probably).
- The account menu in `AppShell.tsx`; the `profiles` table (`preferred_language` etc. from #4).
- Root document/HTML shell in `src/routes/__root.tsx`.

### 3. Scope

**In scope:** dark values for every token, the theme toggle with persistence, the no-flash script, fixes for charts/badges/gradients/auth in dark, a contrast check, the manifest, icons, the service worker (static assets only), the install prompt, mobile checks for Live Calls and Leads.

**Out of scope:** push notifications, full offline data access, native apps.

### 4. What to build, point by point

#### 4.1 Dark theme tokens
1. In `src/styles.css`, define a `.dark { … }` value for **every** token in `:root` (background, foreground, card, popover, primary, secondary, muted, accent, destructive, border, input, ring, chart-1…5, sidebar-*). Use the same hue family, with lighter text and darker surfaces. Aim for AA contrast.
2. Gradients and shadows: dark versions (a softer `shadow-soft`, gradients with less glare).
3. Replace hard-coded colours in components (`bg-white`, `text-gray-900`, `#hex` in charts) with tokens (`bg-background`, `text-foreground`, `var(--chart-1)`). Search: `grep -rn "bg-white\|text-black\|#[0-9a-fA-F]\{6\}" src/`.

#### 4.2 Toggle and persistence
4. `src/lib/theme.tsx`: a `ThemeProvider` with `theme: "system" | "light" | "dark"`, a resolved theme that listens to `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')`, and it applies or removes the `dark` class on `<html>`.
5. Save it to `localStorage` (instant) **and** to `profiles.theme` (follows the user across devices). On sign-in, the profile value wins.
6. **No flash:** an inline script in the HTML `<head>` (in `__root.tsx`) that reads localStorage/system and sets the class **before** the page paints.
7. The toggle in the account menu: a three-option segmented control (Monitor / Sun / Moon icons, `aria-label`s). Also on the Profile page (#4) if it's merged.

#### 4.3 Check every page in both themes
8. Go through every sidebar page, the auth page, the landing page and the dialogs. Fix unreadable text, invisible borders, white flashes in charts, and badges with poor contrast (`StatusBadge` colours need dark variants).
9. Recharts: axis/grid/tooltip colours from tokens; the tooltip background `var(--popover)`.
10. Images or logos that disappear on dark: provide a light version, or add a subtle background.

#### 4.4 PWA
11. `public/manifest.webmanifest`: `name` "Yulabs CRM", `short_name` "Yulabs", `start_url` "/dashboard", `scope` "/", `display` "standalone", `background_color`, `theme_color`, and `icons` 192, 512 and 512 maskable (PNG). Link it in the `<head>` with `<link rel="manifest">`, plus `<meta name="theme-color">` (light and dark via `media`), and the `apple-touch-icon` 180.
12. Icons in `public/icons/` (generated from the logo; keep the maskable icon's safe zone in mind).
13. Service worker `public/sw.js` (hand-written, small) or `vite-plugin-pwa` (check it works with the Lovable/TanStack config first; if unsure, go hand-written):
    - precache the app shell (the offline page, icons, main CSS/JS from the build manifest if practical)
    - **network-first** for navigations, falling back to `/offline.html` ("You're offline. Reconnect to see your calls.")
    - **cache-first** for hashed static assets (`/assets/*`)
    - **never cache** API calls (`/api/*`), Supabase requests or anything with customer data
    - version the cache name and delete old caches on `activate`
14. Register the SW in the client only in production (`import.meta.env.PROD`), after load.
15. **Install prompt:** catch `beforeinstallprompt` and show an "Install app" item in the account menu (Android/desktop Chrome). On iOS Safari, show a one-time hint: "Share → Add to Home Screen".

#### 4.5 Phone width
16. Live Calls and Leads at 375 px: cards instead of wide tables, big tap targets (≥ 44 px), and the sidebar becomes a drawer. Coordinate with #8, which may already do this.

### 5. Data model

```sql
-- 00NN_profile_theme.sql: remember each user's theme
alter table public.profiles add column if not exists theme text not null default 'system'
  check (theme in ('system','light','dark'));
```

### 6. Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `db/migrations/00NN_profile_theme.sql` | **new** |
| `src/styles.css` | dark tokens |
| `src/lib/theme.tsx` | **new**: provider and hook |
| `src/routes/__root.tsx` | no-flash script, manifest/meta links, SW registration |
| `src/components/app/AppShell.tsx` | theme toggle, install item |
| `src/components/app/ThemeToggle.tsx`, `InstallPrompt.tsx` | **new** |
| `public/manifest.webmanifest`, `public/sw.js`, `public/offline.html`, `public/icons/*` | **new** |
| components with hard-coded colours, chart configs | use tokens |
| `src/test/theme.test.ts` | **new** |

### 7. Rules, edge cases, security

- **The service worker never caches API or customer data.** It's a shell cache only.
- No flash of the wrong theme on load or navigation.
- "System" follows OS changes live.
- An old service worker must not trap users on an old version: use a versioned cache, `skipWaiting` + `clients.claim`, and show "New version available, Reload" when an update is waiting.
- AA contrast in both themes.

### 8. Testing

**Unit tests:** theme resolution (system + OS dark → dark; explicit light wins); the localStorage read/write helper; the SW route matcher (a pure function deciding cache / network / never for a URL), which must return "never" for `/api/*` and Supabase URLs.

**Manual:**
1. Toggle System/Light/Dark → it applies instantly; reload → no flash; sign in on another browser → the theme follows the profile.
2. Screenshot every page in dark mode (attach them in the PR).
3. Lighthouse → "Installable" passes; the PWA checks are green.
4. Build and preview: `npm run build && npm run preview` (the SW only registers in production builds).
5. DevTools → Application → Service Workers: registered; Cache Storage contains **no** `/api` responses.
6. Offline (DevTools → Network → Offline) → the offline page shows.
7. **Android** (Chrome): install from the menu → it opens to the dashboard in standalone mode. **iPhone** (Safari): Share → Add to Home Screen → it opens to the dashboard.

```bash
npx vitest run src/test/theme.test.ts
npm run build && npm run preview
```

### 9. Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every page looks right in dark mode (screenshots), with AA contrast
- [ ] System / Light / Dark toggle, saved per user, no flash
- [ ] The app installs on Android and iOS home screens and opens to the dashboard
- [ ] The service worker caches the shell only (never API data); there's an offline page
- [ ] Live Calls and Leads are usable at phone width

### 10. Git workflow for this issue

```bash
git checkout dev && git pull
git checkout -b feature/25-dark-mode-pwa
git add src/styles.css src/lib/theme.tsx src/components/app/ThemeToggle.tsx
git commit -m "Dark mode: tokens, theme provider and toggle"
git push -u origin feature/25-dark-mode-pwa
git fetch origin && git rebase origin/dev && git push --force-with-lease
gh pr create --base dev --title "#25 Dark mode and installable PWA" --body "Closes #25 ..."
```

### 11. In the pull request

- `Closes #25`; the migration to apply
- Light/dark screenshots of the main pages; photos or screenshots of the installed app on a phone

### 12. Settle with the lead before starting

- The dark palette (agree with #8), and the app name/icon for the home screen.
- A hand-written service worker vs `vite-plugin-pwa`.

## #7: API and MCP documentation (with use cases)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | https://github.com/yulabs-in/CRM-Based-Voice-Agents/issues/7 |
| **Assignee** | Kammar Shashank (`KAMMAR-SHASHANK`) |
| **Branch** | `feature/7-api-docs` |
| **PR into** | `dev` |
| **Order** | Shashank's last issue (the skeleton can start any time) |
| **Depends on** | #5 REST API (Charan), #6 MCP server (Tejaswini) |
| **Blocks** | nothing |
| **Size** | ~4–5 days |

### 1. Summary

A documentation page that lets a customer's developer integrate **without asking us anything**: quick start, authentication, every endpoint with copy-able examples, errors, rate limits, MCP setup for three AI clients, and five step-by-step use cases.

### 2. What already exists / your sources

- The #5 PR description: endpoint table, request/response examples, error codes.
- The #6 PR description: tool list and client config snippets.
- UI building blocks: `PageHeader`, cards, `src/components/ui/*`; `auth.tsx` for the visual style.

### 3. Scope

**In scope:** the docs route, layout with a sidebar table of contents, all content below, copy buttons, mobile layout.

**Out of scope:** auto-generated OpenAPI (note it as a follow-up), SDKs.

### 4. What to build, point by point

#### 4.1 Page and layout
1. Agree on the route with the lead: `/docs` (public, best for customers) or `/settings/developers` (signed in). If it's public, put it outside `_authenticated` (e.g. `src/routes/docs.tsx`).
2. Layout: a sticky left sidebar (desktop) with anchors to every section, collapsing to a "Contents" dropdown on mobile. Content max width ~760 px.
3. A `CodeBlock` component (`src/components/docs/CodeBlock.tsx`): language tabs (**curl** | **JavaScript**), monospace, horizontal scroll, and a **Copy** button that shows "Copied" for 2 s.
4. An `Endpoint` component: method badge (GET green, POST blue, PATCH amber), path, required scope chip, description, parameters table, request example, response example, error list.
5. Keep the content in `src/content/docs/*.ts` (plain data/strings), so it's easy to update without touching layout code.
6. When signed in, show a "Create an API key" button that links to Settings → API & MCP.

#### 4.2 Sections (in this order)
7. **Overview:** what the API can do, the base URL (`https://yulabs-crm-1122.netlify.app/api/v1`), JSON only.
8. **Quick start:** (1) create a key in Settings → API & MCP, (2) first request:
   `curl https://…/api/v1/contacts?limit=5 -H "Authorization: Bearer yk_live_…"`, (3) the response explained.
9. **Authentication & scopes:** the Bearer header; a table of every scope and what it allows; key safety (server-side only, never in browser code; revoke if leaked).
10. **Pagination:** `limit`, `cursor`, `next_cursor`, with a loop example in JS.
11. **Errors:** the `{ error: { code, message } }` format; a table of 400/401/403/404/409/429/500 with the cause and the fix.
12. **Rate limits:** 60/min per key, the headers, retry with backoff (a JS snippet).
13. **Endpoints:** one `Endpoint` block for each route in #5 (contacts ×4, leads, deals, calls ×3).
14. **MCP:** what MCP is (2 lines), the server URL, the auth header, and config for **Claude Code**, **Claude Desktop**, **Cursor** (from the #6 PR), plus example questions and the list of tools.
15. **Use cases** (each: goal → what you need → steps → full code → how to check it worked):
    1. *Website enquiries → Contacts:* a form handler (Node/Express or a serverless function) that POSTs to `/contacts`.
    2. *New lead → AI call → read the result:* POST `/calls`, then poll `GET /calls/:id` until `completed`, then read `answers` and `summary`.
    3. *Interested leads → Google Sheet every morning:* a Google Apps Script with `UrlFetchApp`, a time-driven trigger at 9:00 IST, writing rows.
    4. *Ask an AI over MCP:* "Which callers want a consultation this week?" Setup plus the expected answer.
    5. *Deals → external dashboard:* a nightly script that pages through `/deals` and upserts into the dashboard's DB or CSV.
16. **Changelog:** a small dated list ("2026-12: v1 released").

### 5. Data model

None.

### 6. Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/routes/docs.tsx` (or `_authenticated/_app/settings.developers.tsx`) | **new** |
| `src/components/docs/CodeBlock.tsx`, `Endpoint.tsx`, `DocsSidebar.tsx` | **new** |
| `src/content/docs/endpoints.ts`, `use-cases.ts`, `mcp.ts` | **new**: content |
| `src/components/app/AppShell.tsx` | optional "Developers" link |
| `src/test/docs-content.test.ts` | **new** |

### 7. Rules and edge cases

- **Every example must work exactly as written.** Run each one against your local server before the PR.
- Use obviously fake keys (`yk_live_xxxxxxxx`) and fake numbers (`+91 90000 00001`), never real ones.
- Keep request/response examples in sync with the #5 code. If you find a mismatch, raise it on #5, don't paper over it.
- Copy buttons must copy plain text (no line numbers or prompts).

### 8. Testing

**Unit test** (`src/test/docs-content.test.ts`): every endpoint in `endpoints.ts` has a method, path, scope, at least one example, and a valid JSON response example (`JSON.parse` succeeds).

**Manual:**
1. Run every curl and JS example against `npm run dev` with a real local key, and tick each one off in the PR.
2. Run the Apps Script use case against a tunnel URL (`cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8080`).
3. **Hallway test:** a teammate who hasn't used the API does use cases 1 and 2 with only the page. Note where they got stuck, fix it, and say so in the PR.
4. Check at 375 px: code scrolls sideways, the sidebar collapses.

### 9. Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All sections in §4.2 exist, with copy-able curl **and** JS examples
- [ ] Every example was run successfully (checklist in the PR)
- [ ] MCP setup works for Claude Code, Claude Desktop and Cursor as written
